name: vLLM
tagline: An inference and serving engine for large language models.
hook: Requires model evaluations for output-affecting changes and keeps one-off kernel benchmarks out of the test tree.
summary: vLLM combines contribution checks with a GPU-oriented development workflow. The file asks for a test's contract and failure mode before implementation, distinguishes correctness tests from performance work, and routes native builds and security reviews to dedicated guides.

techniques.title: Design the test before writing its setup
techniques.body: The test section asks what the module does, what crosses its boundary, and which failure the test protects against. It then selects the cheapest level that catches that failure.
techniques.quote:
**Design before you write.** Answer four questions first: what is the module
  for, what is its I/O contract, what failure am I guarding against, and what is
  the cheapest level that catches it (unit over integration over e2e)?

techniques.title: Separate kernel performance from correctness coverage
techniques.body: One-off performance work belongs in the kernel benchmark directory. Correctness belongs in the existing pytest suites, so the two kinds of evidence have explicit homes.
techniques.quote:
**No one-off kernel benchmarks in `tests/`.** Put kernel perf work in
  `benchmarks/kernels/`; prove correctness in existing pytest suites.

techniques.title: Require model evaluations when behavior can change
techniques.body: Tests alone do not satisfy the guidance for changes affecting output, accuracy, or serving. The file asks for model evaluations and their results in the PR before a reviewer has to request them.
techniques.quote:
**Run model evals for model-affecting changes.** Search `tests/evals/` or use
  `vllm bench` and include results in the PR — do not wait for reviewers to ask.

techniques.title: Route native builds away from the default editable install
techniques.body: The default install starts with precompiled artifacts. C, C++, and CUDA changes instead follow the incremental compilation guide, making the distinction depend on the edited implementation.
techniques.quote:
For C/C++ or CUDA changes, follow the
[incremental compilation workflow](docs/contributing/incremental_build.md) to
configure and perform incremental builds.

steal: Ask for the test contract and target failure before building fixtures.
Give performance experiments and correctness tests separate homes.
State which behavioral changes require evaluations beyond unit tests.
Distinguish precompiled development installs from native rebuild workflows.
